key_insight: Federated deep learning let two different cohort datasets improve cardiovascular disease risk prediction without sharing patient-level data.
clinical_relevance: This could help health systems build stronger, privacy-preserving risk models across institutions when local data alone are limited.
method: Federated deep survival models were trained across Lifelines and the Rotterdam Study.
The cohorts differed in size, population characteristics, and outcome definitions.
Performance was compared with locally trained models without federation.
evidence_signal: On the Rotterdam Study, the C-statistic improved from 0.728 to 0.739; on Lifelines, it improved from 0.783 to 0.787.
watch_item: Real-world deployment still needs careful handling of differing data definitions, cohort imbalance, and follow-up quality across sites.
paper_title: Federated Deep Learning for Privacy-Preserving Cardiovascular Disease Risk Prediction
